_comment: Core simulation timing and world defaults. Every value here is tunable without touching engine code (spec section 45).

tick._comment: Fixed timestep. The simulation NEVER integrates with a frame delta; time scaling changes how many fixed ticks run per rendered frame, not the size of a tick.
tick._maxStepsPerFrameComment: Upper bound on catch-up work in one frame. When 10x speed cannot keep up, the sim runs in slow motion instead of spiralling.

replay._comment: Snapshot cadence for rewind. A snapshot every N ticks bounds how far the engine must re-simulate to reach an arbitrary point.

lod._comment: Level of detail. These throttle how often a distant CAPTAIN makes a decision, and nothing else. Ballistics, trajectory tracing and penetration are never simplified, because they decide what happens at the moment of a hit and section 39 requires that to be the same wherever the camera is. What counts as distant is the range to the nearest contact the ship's own side is holding — simulation state, deterministic, and the same on every machine. Deciding it from the camera would be the obvious implementation and a disaster: the battle would depend on where the player was looking, two players watching the same action would see different outcomes, and every replay would be wrong.
lod._fireControlComment: Ticks between gunnery solutions per ship, staggered by ship id. A main battery turret trains at a few degrees a second, so re-solving the intercept every tick moves the ordered bearing by under a tenth of a degree — all cost, no effect. Turrets still train every tick; only the solution they are training towards is refreshed less often.
lod._damageControlComment: Damage control, flooding and fire run at a FIXED cadence for every ship, near or far. They are physical rates rather than decision cadences, and throttling them would mean a burning ship put herself out faster or slower depending on where the fighting was.

spatial._comment: Which spatial index a battle uses. Both implementations satisfy the same contract and are asserted to return byte-identical results and produce bit-identical battles, so this is a performance choice and nothing else — see tests/unit/test_spatial_index.gd. 'brute' is the correctness oracle and is worth switching to if a spatial result is ever in doubt.
spatial._cellSizeComment: Side of a grid cell. A few hundred metres puts a handful of ships in a cell at fleet-action densities while keeping a 20 km detection sweep to a few hundred cell lookups rather than a scan of everything afloat.
